---
title: "Examination — the country-analysis poster"
---

The examination for this course is a **poster** on a country or region case study, which
you prepare in groups and present during the poster conference at the end of the semester.

## Content and guiding questions for the poster

Students are expected to prepare a poster (DIN-A0) and to **pitch** it to the other students
during the poster conference at the end of the course (max. 5 minutes per student). Each
student will be asked questions about the content they were responsible for. Students will
prepare the poster together in groups of **up to 3 people**.

The goal of the poster is to present an analysis of the main challenges faced by a specific
country or region, which students selected during the second week of lectures. Make sure you
choose a country or region whose documents are available in a language you understand and
from which you can access the necessary data (see the [data hints](/content/index.qmd#some-hints-on-finding-data)).
In their analysis, students are expected to identify key socio-ecological challenges of the
country or region, describe and evaluate current solution strategies, and critically discuss
these strategies while suggesting improvements.

More precisely, the analysis involves **three major steps**.

**First**, students are expected to **identify a set of challenges** to the country/region,
which they consider essential. They need to justify their choice precisely. Challenges can
refer to economic, social and/or ecological problems, e.g.:

- Excessive reliance on fossil fuels
- Extensive externalization of ecological costs into other countries ('living at the expense
  of others') or serving as a sink for ecological problems caused by other countries (being
  'exploited for the sake of others')
- Problems in ensuring a decent level of well-being for the whole population
- Relevance of national energy poverty
- Excessive levels of income and/or wealth inequalities
- Problems in achieving the SDGs
- Excessive inflation and political polarization
- Problems to remain within planetary boundaries[^leeds]

[^leeds]: You should refer to the data provided by the good life and planetary boundaries working group from Leeds University. See the links to data sources in the [data hints](/content/index.qmd#some-hints-on-finding-data).

It is crucial that you justify why you consider these challenges essential and worth
examining. You also need to be clear about your value system, for example, when arguing that
the current level of inequality in a country is 'unjust.' Students are then expected to explain
how the country or region currently addresses the challenges described above and to critically
analyze the current strategy.

Here are some brief examples (your own analysis should go into much more detail, of course):

- One of the main challenges for **France** is the excessive reliance on nuclear energy. The
  current government does not perceive this as a major problem for various reasons. We believe
  that because of generational justice, water scarcity, and global justice arguments this needs
  to change. Investment in green energy is required and should be financed by a wealth tax.
- One of **Bangladesh's** main challenges is the high poverty rate and gender inequality.
  Currently, the country tries to become more competitive through low prices and environmentally
  harmful activities. This is problematic; the country should focus on building a green technology
  industrial base. International development collaboration is necessary.
- One of **Germany's** main challenges is decarbonizing energy production and consumption. The
  country aims to diversify its energy sources and strongly supports the development, use, and
  import of green hydrogen. Consequently, political leaders and German companies are not only
  promoting domestic green hydrogen production but also importing it from countries mostly in
  the Global South, such as Chile, Morocco, or Nigeria. This approach risks creating social
  injustices and resource exploitation similar to colonialism. Therefore, it is important to
  carefully design these hydrogen partnerships, for example by including sustainability criteria
  for green hydrogen production in the exporting countries, to ensure socio-economic benefits
  are created locally.
- **Morocco** has achieved success in developing renewable energy. One challenge in the Moroccan
  energy transition is dependence on foreign investments and ownership, which creates social
  injustices due to limited socio-economic opportunities for small actors and a lack of involvement
  and participation from rural communities. Supportive measures for small actors, such as
  implementing a feed-in tariff and government support for domestic actors, are necessary.

In the **final step**, students are asked to suggest ways to improve or even redirect the
current strategy. This includes analyzing risks, opportunities, and success factors for the new
approach.

For each step, if you have doubts or questions, please ask us for feedback.

## Examination

The posters need to be printed individually and brought to the class on the day of the poster
presentation. A digital copy of the poster must be uploaded on Moodle **one week before** your
presentation.

The final mark for the course depends on the quality of the students' poster and their
performance during the final poster presentation. The criteria for the evaluation are described
below. The following specifics apply to the overall evaluation of the work:

- A contribution that is not graded as at least *adequate* in dimensions #3 ("formalities"),
  #4 ("clarity and comprehensibility of argument"), #5 ("correctness and accuracy of exposition")
  or #8 ("spelling and grammar") will be graded 5.0.
- If the work receives only a *sufficient* or *satisfactory* rating in dimensions #4 ("clarity
  and comprehensibility of argument") or #5 ("correctness and accuracy of exposition"), the
  overall rating cannot receive a grade better than 'sufficient' (4.0) or 'satisfactory' (3.0).
- If a student provides a certificate for diagnosed dyslexia before submitting the work,
  dimension #8 ("spelling and grammar") will be ignored.

Apart from these special features, the overall rating results from the individual ratings in each
assessment dimension. The "Weight" column shows the relative importance of each dimension for the
overall score. For each dimension, we use an average reference value; special characteristics of
the work may lead to upgrades or downgrades. The overall grade depends on the percentage of
maximum points earned. A work that scores the reference value in each dimension receives a grade
of 2.7. For the points in section I, only the poster itself is considered. For the final scores in
sections II and III, both the poster and the oral presentation are evaluated, with the primary
focus on the poster. Section IV considers only the oral performance.

It is very important that when submitting their poster, groups indicate precisely which student
was mainly responsible for which part of the final work, or which parts were prepared by all
students equally. Depending on how students distribute the work within their group, not all
evaluation dimensions might be relevant for each student. In such cases, the corresponding
dimensions will simply be ignored when computing the final mark.

### Assessment dimensions

**I. Structure and design of the poster** — the entire group receives a joint grade

| #  | Criterion | Weight | Guiding questions |
|:--:|:----------|:------:|:------------------|
| 1 | Structure and outline of the poster content ("red thread") | 3 | Do the individual parts build on each other meaningfully? Is the structure determined by guiding questions? Does each element contribute to answering them? |
| 2 | Design of the poster | 3 | Is the poster visually appealing and easy to read? Do design choices facilitate conveying the key message? |
| 3 | Formalities: consistent layout, correct citation, etc. | 2 | Have the formal requirements been met? Has sufficient and correct citation been given? |

**II. General aspects and formalities** — each student receives an individual grade

| #  | Criterion | Weight | Guiding questions |
|:--:|:----------|:------:|:------------------|
| 4 | Clarity and comprehensibility of the argumentation (logical stringency) | 2 | Are assumptions, mechanisms, and conclusions clearly identified? Do conclusions follow logically? Are normative assumptions made explicit? |
| 5 | Correctness and accuracy of the arguments made | 2 | Are the statements made correct in content and accurately reflected upon? |
| 6 | Extent and adequacy of the literature and data considered | 2 | Is literature incorporated appropriately, scientific, relevant, and balanced? |
| 7 | Precision, systematics, and comprehensibility of the presentation of results | 2 | Were results described systematically and reported comprehensibly? |
| 8 | Spelling & grammar | 1 | Is the work free of spelling and grammatical errors? Is the sentence structure understandable? |
| 9 | Use of tables and graphics | 1 | Are figures and tables used to support the core arguments? |

**III. Specific aspects of the country analysis** — each student receives an individual grade

| #  | Criterion | Weight | Guiding questions |
|:--:|:----------|:------:|:------------------|
| 10 | Justification and explanation of the challenges identified | 3 | Were the main challenges made explicit and adequately justified? Is their background explained well? |
| 11 | Justification and analysis of current solutions | 3 | Are the current solution strategies described and analyzed exhaustively? |
| 12 | Critical assessment of the current strategy and outline of alternatives | 3 | Are current strategies assessed exhaustively, transparently, and convincingly? Are viable suggestions for improvement made? |

**IV. Oral performance** — each student receives an individual grade

| #  | Criterion | Weight | Guiding questions |
|:--:|:----------|:------:|:------------------|
| 13 | Pitch of the poster | 3 | Does the short pitch convey the key take-aways and motivate a closer look? Do students adhere to the 5-minute pitch? |
| 14 | Quality of the answers | 3 | Were the answers correct, to the point, logically consistent, and justified with reference to theory or data? |

::: {.callout-note}
Detailed examples of upgrades and downgrades for each dimension are provided in the full
examination rubric on [Moodle](https://elearning.uni-flensburg.de/moodle/course/view.php?id=17919).
:::
